question: Does the public short-horizon rule add value relative to passive semiconductor exposure under comparable starting allocations?
known_results_before_design: 2022-2025 aggregate, annual and stock gross results already observed; this is retrospective attribution, not a preregistered or prospective test
scope: Summary-only CIZ 2022-2025 gross results; no broker, Trading, group or new WRDS query
primary_comparator: For each selected period, always-long sleeves start with the SAME stock weights as the public rule at that period start. No within-period cross-stock rebalance. Each annual comparator is a separate conditional benchmark; annual comparator returns must not be compounded as one continuous strategy.
decomposition: original_public_minus_original_passive = public_minus_same_weight_passive + same_weight_passive_minus_original_passive. Terms describe holding paths and initial allocations, not causal AI effects or risk-adjusted alpha.
attribution: Stock contributions use public period-start weights. Monthly return contributions use actual month-start wealth weights; monthly increments relative to period-start capital telescope to period return. Do not sum simple monthly percentage returns.
exposure: Mean of daily beginning-of-interval invested dollars divided by public beginning-of-interval total wealth. Not held-name share or an ex-post risk-matching multiplier.
risk: Drawdowns use period-normalized daily close wealth including starting wealth 1. No annualization, significance or deployment claim.
cost_status: Gross only. Existing required crossed quote gate and net-result blocker retained.
